# Slint drive coverage - the ledger of every inventory row (generated by tools/slint_drive_ledger.py, docs/engine-stage4.md 6.47)

Every row of `docs/slint-port-tick.md` against the drive suite (`src/slint/tests/drive/*.txt`, one ctest each, run on the hidden desktop by
`test_slint_drive_run`). **DRIVEN+ASSERTED** = a script operates the control and reads the effect back (the engine's state, the host's
settings half or the control's own value); **DRIVEN** = operated, nothing to read back (the detail says why); **NOT DRIVABLE** = the
scripted input cannot reach it (the detail says why). The authors' word is `src/slint/tests/drive/coverage-<author>.tsv`; the rows not in it are
classified by rule (a readout-like type, a DEFERRED or RELOCATED row). `ctest -R slint_drive_ledger` fails when this file is stale or a row
is unclassified.

## Totals

| rows | DRIVEN+ASSERTED | DRIVEN | NOT DRIVABLE | UNCLASSIFIED |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2190 | 564 | 92 | 1534 | 0 |

Of the 1303 rows that are controls (the 887 readout-like rows left out): 564 asserted, 92 driven without a read-back, 647 not drivable.

NOT DRIVABLE by reason: readout 887, other 217, needs a signal (no fixture) 120, relocated 86, deferred 72, withheld in a bounded run 70, needs hardware 32, no label in the element tree 25, not installed 21, needs a file 3, no plugin fitted 1.

## Every row

### Main window frame — Window layout (how the main window is built)

| # | control | type | class | script | detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cabinet | Brass frame, bevel, four screws, sunk well around everything | NOT DRIVABLE | - | relocated: no cabinet on Workbench: the window ground, hairlines and panels replace the brass frame (BRIEF: restyle allowed) |
| 2 | Title rail | Top strip of the cabinet; replaces the OS title bar (Windows only) | NOT DRIVABLE | - | a container, not a control: its keys are rows 10-12 and the drag is row 13 |
| 3 | Deck (toolbar) | Directly under the rail, full width | NOT DRIVABLE | - | relocated: the 104 px receiver strip |
| 4 | FUNCTION SELECT rail | Left column under the deck | NOT DRIVABLE | - | relocated: the 64 px icon rail + the 296 px sections panel |
| 5 | Centre | Between rail and status column: spectrum, waterfall, pages (, aw.cpp:13463) - inventoried elsewhere. Replaced by the Patch canvas when the PATCH view key is pressed (, aw.cpp:4761) | NOT DRIVABLE | - | a container, not a control: its tabs are rows 68-69 and the spectrum and waterfall rows below |
| 6 | STATUS column | Right column under the deck | NOT DRIVABLE | - | relocated: the 28 px status bar of seven chips; since 6.62 a chip squeezed by a long language gives up its detail first (the detail elides, the tip says it) so the right-hand chips and the two keys stay inside the window |
| 7 | Scope mode | Replaces rail + centre + status column; the deck stays. Entered from a radar/instrument;  leaves it when nothing is being typed and no popup is open (, aw.cpp:20136, Esc at ~20160) - inventoried elsewhere | DRIVEN+ASSERTED | main-tabs-and-rail.txt | click the SCOPE tab; state view == 2 (the instrument entry that also reaches it needs a radar) |
| 8 | Floating windows | Plugin windows, pages, markers, import dialog etc. are separate top-level ImGui windows drawn over the root (, aw.cpp:21884; dialogs list at aw.cpp:4770-4782) | NOT DRIVABLE | - | relocated: pages and plugin windows dock as tabs or tear off (Tab, TornWindow, WindowChrome built; phase-3 content) |

### Main window frame — Title rail (window chrome, Windows only)

| # | control | type | class | script | detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | Window title | readout | NOT DRIVABLE | - | a readout, not a control |
| 10 | Minimise key | button | NOT DRIVABLE | - | would hide the bounded run's window: told not to drive it |
| 11 | Maximise / restore key | button | NOT DRIVABLE | - | would resize the bounded run's window: told not to drive it |
| 12 | Close key | button | NOT DRIVABLE | - | would end the run before its last tick |

| 14 | Rail system menu | context menu | NOT DRIVABLE | - | deferred: Windows' own system menu needs the native handle, which the Slint C++ API does not expose: phase 2 (callback system-menu-requested exists) |
| 15 | Window edges and corners | drag/gesture | NOT DRIVABLE | - | a pointer drag on the window edge: the scripted input has no drag verb |
